readings_ruling: The dispatch asked four questions. All four check out, with two precisions (findings 1 and 2). (1) The printed-form predicates. VoisinageMajorePrinted n (Hilbert.lean:568) is Prop. 3 as printed (l.365-367). It quantifies over every V : Type with a charted structure on S(n), the projective groupoid, T2 and ConnectedSpace, every real k > 0 and every M, and concludes ∃ W ∈ 𝓝 M, IsMajorePart n k W, which is Déf. 4 on a neighbourhood. It omits second countability, so the predicate is formally stronger than the printed statement (finding 2), but the witness is a single point. PseudoLongueurCorpsConvexePrinted n (l.1522) is Prop. 2's three printed assertions over every K with IsCorpsConvexeS n K (Déf. 11, ch1 l.285-287), with the last one read « = 0 ↔ A = B ». Both ↔ 0 < n lemmas are proved, and both n = 0 witnesses are genuine under the paper's own definitions. S(0) = S(ℝ¹) (ch1 l.278) is two antipodal points with the discrete topology. {x} is a strict convex part (F({x}) ∪ {O} is a closed half-line), compact, and open, so it is a convex body (Déf. 11) and its interior is {x}. The only segment of V = {x} is (x, x), so Déf. 2 needs the measure of xx relative to xx, the cross-ratio (x, x, x, x). Déf. 1 (l.262-268) gives that no value. The witnesses therefore rest on Déf. 1's convention exactly as the REPORT says (« through Déf. 1's convention only », OQ-45), and under OQ-45 (b) they disappear. (2) « ne s'annule que sur la diagonale ». Read literally (the zero set is contained in the diagonal), it is weaker than the iff reading, which adds l_V(A, A) = 0. For the principal theorem (n ≥ 1) the iff is proved, so the Lean statement is at least the paper's under either reading: a strengthening of the conclusion, not a narrowing. The iff reading is also the one the paper intends, since 6° (l.250-251, checked on the scan) says « nulle si et seulement si M = N » and 1° says l_V(M, M) = 0. But for the dimension-0 finding the reading decides everything. Under the literal reading Prop. 2 holds for n = 0 (V is one point and l_V never vanishes; hilbertLength_ne_zero). Every assertion of Prop. 2 is then proved in every dimension by NeZero-free lemmas, though no single declaration assembles them (finding 1). The REPORT discloses this: finding 1 is stated conditionally and question 3 says it. (3) The A = B reading is harmless. For A = B « la droite AB » is undefined. Sphere.lineThrough A A ⊆ {A, −A} (lineThrough_self_subset) never meets the frontier, because A is interior and −A ∉ K, so the first assertion is vacuous there and the proof shows it (pseudoLength_eq_projMeasure, by_cases). Under the alternative reading « any chord FF′ through A », the assertion would say l_V(A, A) = log(A, A, F′, F) = log 1 = 0. That is the iff's backward direction (proved for n ≥ 1), and in S(0) no line exists at all. Nothing of the paper's content is lost. (4) The convergence in 5° is the weakest reasonable notion, so the theorem is at least the paper's. propriete_cinq_limsup assumes only that the endpoints converge (along any filter) and that the segments eventually lie in every open set containing (M, N): endpoint convergence plus the upper half of Vietoris convergence. Uniform convergence of chart parametrisations implies both, and so does Hausdorff/Vietoris convergence of the sets with the ordered endpoints converging. So the hypothesis is no stronger than any natural reading. Dropping the set condition would make 5° false, and the REPORT's remark that « endpoints alone would not do » is correct. Example: the Hopf circle (0, ∞)/(x ↦ 2x) ⊂ S(1). The points 1.2 and 1.5 are joined by the segments [1.2, 1.5] and [0.75, 1.2] of its cover, both injective in V, with pseudo-lengths log 1.25 and log 1.6. A constant sequence on the second, with the first as limit, breaks the limsup inequality. propriete_cinq is the printed proof's « tout segment assez voisin » form, with the same neighbourhood notion.

labels.label: bzprop:c2s2p2_pseudo_longueur_corps_convexe
labels.notes: Correctly UNMARKED and status partial. The only added hypothesis is [NeZero n], disclosed (checklist ⚠ strengthened, SCOPE, REPORT hypotheses « added »). pseudo_longueur_corps_convexe (Hilbert.lean:1457) has the hypotheses IsCorpsConvexeS n K (Déf. 11) and V = corpsInterior K = Opens.interior K with Mathlib's charted structure on an open set. They are the paper's « V̄ un corps convexe de S(n) d'intérieur V ». frontier K is « la frontière de V̄ », K being closed. The conclusions, hypothesis by hypothesis against l.306-313 (checked against the scan, journal p. 250 = PDF p. 23). (0) Every segment of V from A to B is (A, B) ∩ V, so l_V is a function of the pair and hilbertLength K is l_V. This makes « l_V(A, B) est une fonction … sur V × V » meaningful. (1) For A ≠ B, F ≠ F′ exist with lineThrough A B ∩ frontier K = {F, F′} (the paper's presupposition, proved; exists_frontier_pair adds A, B ∈ )F, F′(). (2) For EVERY segment Sg from A to B and EVERY such pair F ≠ F′, pseudoLength n Sg A B = projMeasure F A B F′, the measure of AB relative to FF′ (CrossRatio.lean:484, argument order A A′ B′ B). Both labellings of F, F′ are covered (projMeasure_reverse, projMeasure_swap), so the Lean statement does not depend on which frontier point is named F. (3) Continuous on V × V into EReal. For n ≥ 1 the function is finite (hilbertLength_lt_top), and continuous_hilbertLength_toReal gives the real-valued form. (4) hilbertLength K A B = 0 ↔ A = B, at least the paper's under either reading (readings_ruling 2). The line AB is Sphere.lineThrough A B = s(span{a, b} − {O}), a line of Déf. 4 for A ≠ B, B ≠ −A (isLine_lineThrough). Not vacuous: the hypotheses are satisfied by every convex body of S(n), n ≥ 1, and the conclusions are substantive. Dimension-free pieces as claimed (no NeZero): pseudoLength_eq_projMeasure, exists_frontier_pair, continuous_hilbertLength, hilbertLength_ne_zero, isProjSegment_corpsInterior_iff. Dimension 0: pseudoLongueurCorpsConvexePrinted_iff is proved, and the witness {x} ⊆ S(0) is genuine under Déf. 1's convention (readings_ruling 1). It is conditional on the iff reading (readings_ruling 2, finding 1). Findings against the paper. The l.316 gap is true: « F, F′ dépendent continûment de A, B » gives nothing at (A, A), where the line AB is undefined and F, F′ have no limit. Continuity there needs l_V(A′, B′) → 0, a uniform estimate (the frontier stays at positive distance from A, so the cross-ratio tends to 1). The statement is unaffected, and the REPORT says so. Routing: if OQ-45 (a), mark Benzecri.pseudo_longueur_corps_convexe as is. See finding 1 for the literal-reading branch.

labels.label: bzprop:c2s2p3_voisinage_majore
labels.notes: Correctly UNMARKED and status partial. voisinage_majore (Hilbert.lean:559): for every V with [TopologicalSpace V] [ChartedSpace (S n) V] [HasGroupoid V (projGroupoid n)] (universe-polymorphic, no T2, connectedness or countability, disclosed as ⚠ weakened), [NeZero n] (disclosed ⚠ strengthened), every real k > 0 and every M : V, ∃ W ∈ 𝓝 M, IsMajorePart n k W. IsMajorePart is the strict library's Déf. 4 (Mesure.lean:329): any two points of W are joined by a segment inside W that is majorised by k in V (Déf. 2, every compatible chart quantified). « voisinage » is a filter neighbourhood, Bourbaki's sense. exists_isOpen_isMajorePart gives an open W. Hypotheses are no stronger than the paper's apart from n ≥ 1, and the conclusion is exactly the paper's (l.365-367, checked against the scan, p. 251 = PDF p. 24). Not vacuous: V = S(n) satisfies the hypotheses. Dimension 0: not_isMajorePart_dim_zero holds on every V charted on S(0), because every segment there is a point and Déf. 1 gives (x, x, x, x) no value. The witness in voisinageMajorePrinted_iff is the open set {x} of S(0), a one-point space: T2, connected and second countable. The failure is genuine under Déf. 1's convention, and it would disappear under OQ-45 (b), which OQ-45's text already names for Prop. 3. The predicate omits second countability (finding 2). Finding against the paper (l.371-372): true. 6° makes l_V < k on a product neighbourhood of (M, M). Déf. 4 also needs the joining segment to lie in W, which needs W chosen convex (for instance a small convex neighbourhood in an affine chart). The step is easy but left implicit. The statement is unaffected, and the Lean proof does exactly this in one chart (exists_nhds_projMeasure_lt). Routing: if OQ-45 (a), mark Benzecri.voisinage_majore as is. Under (b) or (c), partial.
